title: Latitude, longitude & time zones
examples: How do I find coordinates on a map?
If it is noon here, what time is it in London?
What is the difference between latitude and longitude?

explain.say: Today we learn about coordinates on a map.
Now let me show you the real thing in 3D: latitude and longitude. Look at the equator, the prime meridian and the latitude lines. Tap any part, and I will tell you what it does.
Latitude lines run across the Earth like parallels.
Longitude lines run up and down the Earth like meridians.
Coordinates tell a precise location using both numbers.
The Earth is divided into time zones for timekeeping.
If you move east, the time gets later by hours.

faq.q: What is the difference between latitude and longitude?
faq.a: Latitude measures how far north or south you are from the Equator. Longitude measures how far east or west you are from the Prime Meridian.
asks: What do lat and long measure?
Which line is horizontal on a map?

faq.q: How do I calculate the time difference between two places?
faq.a: You need to find the difference in degrees of longitude and divide that by sixteen to find the hours difference. Remember to check if you are moving east or west.
asks: If I go east, do I add or subtract time?
What is the rule for time zone math?

faq.q: Is the Equator always zero degrees latitude?
faq.a: Yes, the Equator is the imaginary line marking zero degrees latitude. It divides the Earth into the Northern and Southern Hemispheres.
asks: What line is at the middle of the Earth?

faq.q: Does the International Date Line change?
faq.a: The International Date Line is generally at 180 degrees longitude. It marks where the date officially changes day to day.
asks: What is the date change line?

faq.q: Do I always use the Prime Meridian when calculating time?
faq.a: Yes, the Prime Meridian, at zero degrees longitude, is the reference point for calculating time differences worldwide. All time zones relate back to it.
asks: What is the main reference point for time?
Where does time calculation start from?

facts: Latitude lines are parallel to the Equator.
Longitude lines converge at the North and South Poles.
The Earth takes approximately 24 hours to rotate 360 degrees.
Time zones are based on the Earth's rotation and longitude.

quiz.say: A location at 40 degrees North and 74 degrees West is best described by:
quiz.why: Coordinates use both latitude (North/South) and longitude (East/West) to pinpoint a spot.

wrong.0: A time zone name describes the local time, not the exact physical location.
wrong.2: Latitude only tells you how far north or south you are, not east or west.
wrong.3: Longitude only tells you how far east or west you are, not north or south.

quiz.say: If a place is 60 degrees east of a location at 0 degrees, the time difference is:
quiz.why: You divide 60 degrees by 15 degrees per hour, which equals four hours.

wrong.0: You should not multiply the degrees by the hours; you must divide.
wrong.1: The answer needs to be in time units, like hours, not degrees.
wrong.2: Any change in longitude means there must be a corresponding time change.

quiz.say: What must you do when travelling west across the Prime Meridian?
quiz.why: Moving west means you are behind the reference point, so you subtract time.

wrong.0: Adding time suggests you are moving forward or eastwards.
wrong.1: The Earth is constantly turning, so time must change with longitude.
wrong.2: While the date might change at the date line, the time also changes gradually.
